data.title: Democrats probe whether Lutnick helped Cantor Fitzgerald avoid Nvidia-linked losses
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Democratic lawmakers have opened a probe into whether US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick used his office to help investment firm Cantor Fitzgerald, which is controlled by his sons, avoid losses stemming from scrutiny of AI chip firm Nvidia's ( NVDA ) ties to a Chinese firm, according to a letter reviewed by Reuters.

In the letter dated November 17, House Democrats notified Brandon Lutnick, chairman of Cantor Fitzgerald and Howard Lutnick's son, that they are requesting information to ascertain if any actions taken by the commerce secretary were "improperly influenced by Cantor Fitzgerald's holdings or business interests."

The lawmakers - US Representatives Jamie Raskin of Maryland, Gregory Meeks of New York and Sydney Kamlager-Dove of California - asked if concerns about Cantor Fitzgerald's "financial exposure, business relationships, or contracts with or commitments to foreign governments" influenced Secretary Lutnick's refusal to add Chinese firm Megaspeed to the Commerce Department's trade blacklist for certain technology or require a license for the export of advanced AI chips to the company.

The US puts companies on its trade blacklist that it has determined pose risks to US national security or foreign policy.

"The Secretary has fully complied with the terms of his ethics agreement, including all divestiture and recusal requirements, and will continue to do so. He has divested all financial interests in Cantor Fitzgerald, Newmark, and BGC," a Commerce spokesperson said in a statement in response to the letter, which was first reported by the Financial Times.

Megaspeed has been in the spotlight after reports that Nvidia's ( NVDA ) former CEO, Jensen Huang, had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy.

Cantor Fitzgerald denied the lawmakers' claims, saying in an emailed statement it holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia ( NVDA ), and that its Nvidia ( NVDA ) holdings arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients. The firm also said it has no role in US export control or blacklist decisions.

Earlier this month, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said four government agencies had favored putting Megaspeed on a trade blacklist known as the Entity List but the Commerce Department, which was in charge, had not.

"If Secretary Bessent is now writing export-control rules and Attorney General Blanche is investigating violators, why hasn't Secretary Lutnick been implementing export controls?" Democratic Senator Maria Cantwell said on Wednesday. "Who is responsible for putting Megaspeed on the Entity List?"

 House Energy and Commerce chair US Representative Brett Guthrie, a Kentucky Republican, separately asked Nvidia ( NVDA ) interim CEO Colette Kress, Lutnick and Commerce official Jeff Kessler to give briefings to lawmakers on reports about Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.

US Senator Tim Scott, a South Carolina Republican who chairs the Senate Banking Committee, said he wanted Lutnick and Jensen Huang to testify publicly. "We have the power of subpoena if they don't come voluntarily," Scott said on CNBC.

(Reporting by David Shepardson in Washington and Rishabh Jaiswal in Bengaluru; additional reporting by Ruchika Khanna, Jaspreet Singh and Ananya Palyekar in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar and Sanjeev Miglani)

data.title: Factory Expands Collaboration with Microsoft to Bring Autonomous Software Engineering to Enterprises
data.description:
Enterprises can deploy Factory in their Microsoft Azure environment and keep work connected across GitHub, Azure DevOps, Microsoft Teams, and more.

SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Factory, a leader in autonomous software engineering, is expanding its collaboration with Microsoft to give enterprises greater flexibility to deploy self-improving software factories. Organizations can run Factory within their Microsoft Azure environment, using existing code, identity, and governance systems.

"Regulated enterprises require autonomy without giving up control of their code," said Matan Grinberg, co-founder and CEO of Factory. "Many of our customers run on Microsoft Azure, GitHub, and Microsoft Teams. Our collaboration with Microsoft enables us to solve their hardest engineering problems inside the environment and controls they trust."

Built for Azure

Factory offers customers complete deployment control within their Azure environment and existing identity, network, and source-control systems. Droids, Factory’s software development agents, run in Azure, including customer-controlled Azure Virtual Network (VNet) environments. With Factory’s self-hosted orchestrator for agent sandboxes and provisioning backend, OpenCompute, agent workloads stay in the customer’s environment, on their Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters or VNet. This allows Droids to use models served through Microsoft Foundry, giving enterprises the same model choice and governance already available in their Azure environments. Droids can then open pull requests, respond to comments, and act on CI results in GitHub or Azure DevOps, within existing review rules and approvals.

From issue to resolution

Droids take engineering work from the first report to merged code. Organizations can hand off issues from Jira, Linear, or GitHub, or route production alerts to Factory. Droids triage each item, investigate the root cause, write and test a fix, and open a pull request for human approval, or even automate the final merge based on customer-controlled preferences.

Security follows the same path. Droids review pull requests in GitHub for security issues, tracing changed data flows and posting validated findings with severity and suggested fixes. Organizations can also run scheduled full-codebase audits, and Droids can carry each finding through to a tested fix.

Factory now uses Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) for OS Containment

Factory protection now extends to the developer’s machine. With support for Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), every command a Droid runs executes inside a container that can access only the files and network destinations a team approves, and the operating system enforces those limits. IT teams manage these policies through Microsoft Intune, the same way they manage the rest of their devices.

Droids in Microsoft Teams

Users can mention @Factory in a Teams chat or channel to hand off tasks to Factory for seamless completion. Factory works in standard and private channels, group chats, and one-on-one chats, leveraging earlier messages as context.

A self-improving software factory

Factory enables autonomous engineering for the enterprise through self-improving software factories deployed across the software development lifecycle, from planning to deployment. Engineers set goals and govern outcomes, while Droids execute. Signals from code review, testing and CI, production incidents, and delivery analytics feed back into Factory, improving the system over time.

Availability

Factory is available today in Microsoft Marketplace, and eligible purchases count toward a customer’s Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment (MACC), centralizing procurement through their existing Microsoft relationship.

"Enterprises are asking how to apply agents to software development safely and at scale," said Kyle Daigle, Chief Operating Officer at GitHub and Chief Marketing Officer of Developer at Microsoft. "Our expanded collaboration with Factory gives customers a governed path to deploy agents across the software development lifecycle on Microsoft Azure, complementing the software development workflows and enterprise AI governance capabilities GitHub already provides.”

Customers can contact their Microsoft account team or reach Factory at sales@factory.com. To learn more, visit Factory in Microsoft Marketplace.

About Factory

Factory builds model-agnostic AI coding agents for the enterprise. The Factory platform enables organizations to design their own software factories and deploy them in the most secure environments.

Customers include NVIDIA, Blackstone, T-Mobile, Adyen, Royal Bank of Canada, and more. Factory was founded in 2023 by Matan Grinberg and Eno Reyes and is headquartered in San Francisco. Investors include Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, Menlo Ventures, NEA, Nvidia, J.P. Morgan, and Insight Partners. To learn more, visit factory.com.

data.title: MCNC Chief Operating Officer Tommy Jacobson receives Order of the Long Leaf Pine
data.description:
Broadband and networking pioneer honored with North Carolina's highest civilian recognition for more than three decades of public service and leadership

RESEARCH TRIANGLE PARK, N.C., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tommy Jacobson, Senior Vice President and Chief Operating Officer of MCNC, today has been awarded the Order of the Long Leaf Pine, the most prestigious honor presented by the Governor of North Carolina for exemplary service to the state.

The award recognizes Jacobson's more than 32 years of dedicated leadership in expanding high-speed connectivity, closing the digital divide, and laying the technological foundation for North Carolina's schools, universities, health care systems, and rural communities. 

His career of service began in the summer of 1993 when he joined MCNC – a technology non-profit established in 1980 – as a student intern prior to his senior year at NC State University. After graduating in 1994 with a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering, he went on to embody the university's "Think and Do" ethos across three decades of executive, operational, and engineering leadership.

As the chief architect of the North Carolina Research and Education Network (NCREN), Jacobson oversaw the design, deployment, and operational resilience of middle-mile broadband infrastructure serving nearly 1,000 community anchor institutions. Today, the network spans more than 4,500 miles across all 100 North Carolina counties, delivering high-speed connectivity and cybersecurity services to millions of users.

Throughout his career, Jacobson's major milestones have helped transform North Carolina:

  • Golden LEAF Rural Broadband Initiative (2010–2013): Jacobson spearheaded the historic $144 million infrastructure deployment funded through federal Broadband Technology Opportunities Program (BTOP, installing more than 2,600 miles of fiber across 82 counties ahead of schedule and under budget.

  • HERO Project (High-Speed Economies for Rural Opportunity): Completed in August 2026 under Jacobson's direction, the project delivered critical middle-mile investments to central and southeastern North Carolina, expanding affordable broadband to historically underserved rural areas.

  • Hurricane Helene (2024): Drawing on deep ties to his native Western North Carolina, Jacobson led emergency round-the-clock restoration efforts, deploying tactical fiber routes through harsh conditions and mountain terrain to restore critical communications for first responders, hospitals, and municipal operations.

Leaders across North Carolina's technology and education community praised Jacobson's recognition:

"What distinguishes his leadership is not his technical and operational command alone, but his ability to align state agency priorities with higher education needs and turn them into cohesive, high-impact outcomes for communities in every corner of North Carolina."
– Tracy Doaks, President and CEO, MCNC

"Tommy Jacobson represents the highest ideal of state leadership and public service. His legacy lives in the thousands of miles of fiber connecting our schools, universities, hospitals, and communities."
– Nathaniel S. Denny, Secretary and State CIO, N.C. Department of Information Technology

"He has spent his career quietly building the critical digital foundation that links our schools, universities, hospitals, and rural communities—never seeking the spotlight, only results."
– Keith Werner, CIO at Appalachian State University (2016 Order of the Long Leaf Pine recipient)

"Tommy's executive stewardship includes his technical and operational mastery, and his strategic vision to align state agency priorities and higher education needs into cohesive, high-impact outcomes for every community in North Carolina."
– Dr. Marc Hoit, Vice Chancellor for IT and CIO at NC State University

"Thirty-two years later, directly as a result of Tommy's leadership, engineering acumen, focus and energy, North Carolina has the most impactful Research and Education Network in our country! Bar none."
– Edward T. Carney, chairman of WhiteStar Communications; former chair of MCNC Board of Directors

"There is no one person more responsible for these advancements than Tommy Jacobson. Tommy led the effort to secure $144 Million in funding to build today's version of the North Carolina Research and Education Network; he engineered the network and oversaw construction of the network."
– Joseph A. Freddoso, former President and CEO of MCNC (2012 Order of the Long Leaf Pine recipient)

"The builds were complicated, multi-year, and filled with the complexities of any project of this size. There is no doubt in my mind that it was due to his efforts that both projects were completed early and under budget."
– Patricia L. Moody, retired Chief Financial Officer at MCNC

Jacobson's dedication to public service runs deep in his family, joining his brother, Steve, who received the Order of the Long Leaf Pine about a decade ago. Throughout his life and career, he has carried the fighting spirit of legendary NC State men's basketball coach Jim Valvano, leaning on his famous mantra, "Don't Give Up... Don't Ever Give Up." Today, Jacobson lives in Burlington with his wife, Pam, a retired educator, and he has two children, Alyssa and Evan.

About MCNC
MCNC is a 501(c)(3) non-profit client-focused technology organization. Founded in 1980, MCNC owns and operates the North Carolina Research and Education Network (NCREN), one of America's longest-running regional research and education networks. With over 45 years of innovation, MCNC provides high-performance services for education, research, libraries, healthcare, public safety, and other community anchor institutions throughout North Carolina. NCREN is the fundamental broadband infrastructure for over 850 of these institutions including all public K-20 education in North Carolina. As one of the nation's premier middle-mile fiber backbone networks, MCNC leverages NCREN to customize protected Internet, cybersecurity services, and related applications for each client while supporting private service providers in bringing cost-efficient connectivity to rural and underserved communities in North Carolina.

Visit www.mcnc.org. MCNC Social: Facebook, X, YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram.

data.title: GTA VI frenzy spotlights potential insurance risks lurking in digital infrastructure
data.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - Millions of gamers around the world have logged on for the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI," arguably the century's most anticipated video game, offering a glimpse of the vast, interconnected digital infrastructure the global economy increasingly relies on.

No major disruption is expected from the rollout. But the scale of demand around one of the gaming industry's biggest releases underscores a broader risk for insurers: a failure at a shared cloud, payments or technology provider could affect thousands of businesses at once.

After 13 years in development and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, 'Grand Theft Auto VI' began rolling out globally on Thursday, drawing the kind of attention that few entertainment releases ever command.

But the fervour also underscores how much modern businesses depend on the digital infrastructure that makes such mass online activity possible, and the risks insurers face when that infrastructure fails.

"A launch of the scale of GTA VI is effectively a built-in stress test of the shared digital economy infrastructure," said Marcos Alvarez, managing director at Morningstar DBRS.

Insurers cover businesses against financial losses stemming from disruptions to their operations, including some caused by technology failures.

As companies increasingly rely on the same cloud providers, payment systems and digital platforms, a single outage could trigger claims from multiple policyholders at once, amplifying exposure.

Despite the frenzy surrounding the launch, any disruption on launch day or in the days that follow would not necessarily spell disaster for insurers, industry experts said.

"The recent technology outages have been a case in point with the gap between the economic cost and the actual insured loss being quite large due to policy limits, retentions, waiting periods, and coverage exclusions," Alvarez added.

Business interruption could be a major source of claims, but coverage could also extend to costs associated with data recovery, system restoration, cyberattacks and outages at third-party technology providers, depending on the policy.

"This is an area that is evolving rapidly for the insurance industry. Insurers are refining how they assess, model and manage these interconnected exposures," said Loretta Worters, a spokesperson for the Insurance Information Institute.

"That means looking beyond an individual company's cybersecurity protections to understand its reliance on third-party providers, the concentration of those dependencies across their portfolios and the potential for a single event to generate losses across multiple policyholders."

​

(Reporting by Manya Saini in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid)

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks slip with Nvidia, dollar ticks higher
data.description:
(Updates prices, recasts first paragraph, adds comments throughout)

* Nvidia ( NVDA ) sales forecast tops expectations but shares fall

* Dollar index hits fresh 19-month high

* Oil prices slide on larger-than-expected inventories

By Rodrigo Campos

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - A gauge of global stocks fell in choppy trading on Wednesday after Nvidia's ( NVDA ) quarterly results and ahead of Anthropic's market debut, while the dollar's strength also weighed on sentiment.

The dollar strengthened to a fresh 19-month high after US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC the central bank needs to either approve a half-point interest rate hike at its December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027.

Mining stocks dragged European shares lower, while Nvidia's ( NVDA ) results initially helped Asian shares, with Korea's Kospi up 2% overnight. But the Nvidia ( NVDA ) rally fizzled and the stock was down 2.4% after rising as much as 2.7%.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board dismissed the idea of rehiring former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week. The company forecast sales ahead of Wall Street targets on Tuesday.

"The central question Nvidia ( NVDA ) faces is not related to this earnings report ... it's more about what the company may look like in 3-5 years without a visionary leader like Jensen and as competition from other chipmakers takes shape," said Jay Peters, portfolio manager at NewEdge Wealth.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.84% to 50,334.82, the S&P 500 eased 0.07% to 7,335.43 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.46% to 24,439.22.

MSCI's gauge of global stocks fell 0.34% to 1,075.82 and the pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.03%. Emerging market stocks eased 0.13% and Japan's Nikkei rose 0.28%.

The next health check on the AI industry will come as Anthropic prepares to price its shares on Wednesday ahead of its market debut.

DOLLAR UP, OIL DOWN

In currencies, the dollar strengthened as Waller's comments and recent economic data cemented expectations for an interest rate hike next month.

"The Federal Reserve seems at the moment to be very determined to hike interest rates and maybe even aggressively do so," said Juan Perez, senior director of trading at Monex USA in Washington. "That's the belief right now that's carrying the US dollar."

The dollar index rose 0.19% to 103.81, with the euro down 0.24% at $1.0971.

In commodities markets, crude prices fell after US crude and fuel inventories rose more than expected, adding to expectations of a supply surplus.

US crude fell 4.39% to $82.23 a barrel and Brent dropped to $90.93 per barrel, down 2.37%.

Spot gold fell 2.86% to $3,739.66 an ounce and spot silver lost 4.72% to $45.16 an ounce. Copper declined 4.69% to $12,606.00 a ton.

US Treasury yields were slightly lower as oil prices dropped, dragging inflation expectations lower.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 3.87 basis points to 5.064% from 5.103% late on Tuesday, while the 30-year bond yield fell 4.49 basis points to 5.414% from 5.459%.

* AI tools help reveal vulnerabilities in software

By AJ Vicens

Nov 18 (Reuters) - While the causes of recent disruptions to the way people work, access bank accounts and travel remain unclear, increased efforts to rapidly patch newly discovered vulnerabilities in the AI age are likely a major factor, according to cybersecurity experts and US officials.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking to reporters in Manila this week, said company patching efforts are, at times, "creating short-term disruption in the way the system works."

Patches are software and operating system updates intended to fix security vulnerabilities found within a program or product.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told a House of Representatives Homeland Security Committee hearing on worldwide threats Wednesday that there is so far no indication that the tech outages are related. But Clayton said the speed and level of capability of computer systems are "increasing substantially," so legacy computer systems and equipment that already were old are aging much more quickly.

The advent of easily accessible AI tools and large language models has supercharged the discovery of vulnerabilities in software. Microsoft ( MSFT ) this month has addressed more than 1,200 software vulnerabilities, nearly 20 times higher than in the same month a year ago, according to cybersecurity firm Qualys ( QLYS ).

At least one major bank was rushing to address a wave of recent patches and there is a lot of work needed, a source at the bank said, speaking on condition of anonymity.

"AI has made finding critical vulnerabilities fast and cheap, and the number of flaws that demand immediate patching has grown with it," said Yuval Itzchakov, CTO and co-founder of autonomous offensive security company A Security.

"Emergency patches go into core infrastructure within hours, often without the full testing cycle, and they are intrusive by design: they change runtimes, kernels and network components that everything else depends on. That speed and scale of change is itself a source of failure," Itzchakov said.

Josh Bressers, director of coordinated vulnerability disclosure at cybersecurity firm VulnCheck, said that in 2026 there have been 100,000 publicly disclosed vulnerabilities, tracked by industry as Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures, or CVEs. Of those, Bressers said, 1,363 were known to have been exploited in the real world.

"Given tight resources for defenders, understanding which vulnerabilities need attention first is critical," Bressers wrote in a LinkedIn post. "Not all vulnerabilities are created equal."

Anne Neuberger, general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, said that AI is helping attackers find and weaponize vulnerabilities, but is a more "valuable friend" to those tasked with defending key computer networks.

"AI is enabling enterprises to find 10 times more vulnerabilities," said Neuberger, who served as deputy national security adviser under former President Joe Biden and led incident response to serious national incidents. "And when patching at scale, some can cause problems."

Ronald Gestiehr, director of wealth management at Luttner Financial, said technology has made banking "incredibly convenient, and while occasional outages can be frustrating I don't believe the outages will have a significant impact on consumer confidence or change how most people manage their money."

"Financial institutions have invested heavily in technology and security, and, unfortunately, occasional disruptions will happen," Gestiehr said. "What matters most is how quickly those issues are identified, resolved and communicated to customers."

(Reporting by AJ Vicens in Detroit, and Nupur Anand and Saeed Azhar in New York; Editing by Will Dunham)

data.title: US pending home sales tumble to record low in October
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Contracts to purchase previously owned US homes plunged to a record low in October as higher mortgage rates suppressed demand for housing.

The pending home sales index dropped 4.7% to 63.0 last month, the lowest level since the series started in 2001, the National Association of Realtors said on Wednesday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast that contracts, which become sales after a month or two, would fall 2.0%. October marked the second straight month of large decreases.

Pending home sales declined 16.7% year over year in October. Sales fell during the month in all four regions.

"Two consecutive months of record-low pending contracts point to very sluggish fourth-quarter home sales closings, and annual existing home sales could be the lowest since the mid-1990s," said Lawrence Yun, the NAR's chief economist.

The NAR last week reported a drop in home resales to the lowest level in more than 16 years in October.

Mortgage rates have remained elevated as the US-Israeli war with Iran drags on. The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.18% last week, after jumping to near a three-year high of 7.40% in mid-October, data from mortgage finance firm Freddie Mac showed.

data.title: Nvidia retreats, weighs on AI stocks as strong outlook fails to dispel Huang uncertainty
data.description:
By Anhata Rooprai and Shashwat Chauhan

Nov 18 (Reuters) - Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares reversed premarket gains on Wednesday and dragged down several AI-linked stocks as initial relief over the chip giant's blockbuster forecast faded amid persistent uncertainty caused by co-founder Jensen Huang's abrupt departure last week.

The stock's retreat showed strong demand for Nvidia's ( NVDA ) chips had steadied confidence but not fully restored it in a sector battered by the leadership crisis at the company at the center of the AI ecosystem.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) fell nearly 2%, after premarket gains of as much as 3%. If sustained, the decline would erase more than $80 billion in market value, on top of the roughly $2 trillion lost between its October record and Tuesday's close.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 has shed about $1.94 trillion in market value so far in November, as investors reassessed lofty AI valuations alongside concerns over China, data center spending and tighter regulation.

"We believe yesterday's results have stabilized sentiment and put a floor under the recent AI selloff, but they have postponed rather than permanently cured investor anxiety," said Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint.

The next test of the AI trade will come later on Wednesday as Anthropic prepares to price its public offering, which could value the frontier lab at up to $1.4 trillion.

The stock's slip comes as an ongoing CEO search, an independent investigation and a Wall Street Journal report that the US Securities and Exchange Commission was also investigating the company weigh on sentiment across AI stocks.

On Wednesday, Nvidia ( NVDA )-backed neoclouds CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius ( NBIS ), chipmakers AMD, Broadcom ( AVGO ) and Intel ( INTC ) as well as data center, storage, photonics and server stocks were mixed, with some declining between 0.2% and 6%.

The AI trade has also been tested since the Democrats' sweeping midterm wins stoked fears of tougher regulation of data center buildouts, sending the tech-heavy Nasdaq into correction territory earlier this month.

BOARD SAYS NO TO HUANG

Nvidia ( NVDA ) Chairman Harvey Jones ruled out reinstating Huang despite his offer to return. Heidrick & Struggles is leading the search for a permanent CEO among both internal and external candidates.

The stock might struggle to climb further until the company names a permanent CEO and the new leadership shows it can deliver planned products, HSBC analysts said.

Interim CEO Colette Kress has said it was "business as usual," citing customer and supplier support. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) forecast offered the clearest evidence yet that the upheaval has not delayed its product roadmap or weakened demand.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) fourth-quarter revenue forecast beat analysts' estimates, while the company also raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to about 75%, saying demand continued to exceed supply.

Third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $115.84 billion, marking a 17th consecutive estimate beat, according to LSEG data.

Adjusted gross margin reached 74.9%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) expects it to bottom between 71% and 72% this quarter as higher supply costs bite, before recovering to between 72% and 73% in fiscal 2028.

"Strong earnings have bought management time," Saxo strategist Charu Chanana said.

CHINA DISAPPEARS FROM OUTLOOK

China contributed $2.4 billion in licensed Hopper data-center sales during the quarter, but Nvidia ( NVDA ) assumed no such shipments in its current forecast and said it was no longer shipping those products to the country.

Management said the outlook considered current US export controls, although it was still studying parts of the new rules announced on Monday, while demand elsewhere was expected to absorb the loss of China sales.

"Kress also provided confident answers around Commerce rules, citing that demand is far exceeding supply and that Nvidia ( NVDA ) is studying the rules around the chip delivery to other countries," said Christopher Brown, vice president of investments at Synovus, which holds Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares.

"We just need to understand that demand is not the same as legal ability to ship."

(Reporting by Shashwat Chauhan and Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru, additional reporting by Avinash P; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Options on Anthropic shares could begin trading as soon as Monday, giving investors a new way to wager on the AI company's prospects as market participants expect heavy interest.

Cboe Global Markets expects to list the contracts two business days after the stock begins trading, pending industry readiness. "The Anthropic IPO could be yet another catalyst, bringing a new wave of investors and trading activity to the options market," said Rob Hocking, Cboe's global head of derivatives. "It's great to see investor education driving this growth, as more people learn how options let them define their risk. An exciting trend and one we expect to continue." 

The Claude developer is expected to price its IPO later on Wednesday, and the shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday.  

"We expect significant interest in Anthropic options once they list," said Garrett DeSimone, head quant at OptionMetrics. "The combination of AI-driven enthusiasm and the lottery-like payoff profile typical of IPOs are likely to draw investors immediately. As one of the most concentrated pure-play exposures to AI, the stock is also likely to be highly volatile."

Interest in Anthropic options could exceed the interest in SpaceX options earlier this year, said Ophir Gottlieb, chief executive of Capital Market Laboratories, citing oversubscription that is pushing the company's valuation higher and could invite various positioning ahead of the deal, as well as the market backdrop.

"The AI trade is melting down," Gottlieb said. "Many feel it is overdone, while many others feel it's the popping of a bubble. Whenever there is such opposing views in a heated market, we get a lot of option positioning."

Options give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell shares at a set price within a certain period. They offer investors a cheaper way to gain exposure to a stock and to express their views on both short-term price moves and longer-term positioning.

Anthropic's $64 billion IPO has drawn stronger early institutional demand than the offering of SpaceX, with the book six times oversubscribed last week, Reuters previously reported.

The IPO has drawn anticipation from investors, with Wall Street rolling out products tied to the stock, hosting client events and giving away merchandise ahead of the AI company's potentially record launch.

data.title: Tellus App Brings Account Context and an AI Support Analyst Into Chatwoot
data.description:
Tellus connected its in-app chat to a self-hosted, open-source customer support workspace. By October, first replies during support hours came 45% faster than before the switch, while conversation volume grew about 30%.

MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. and SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tellus App, Inc. ("Tellus"), a financial and real estate technology company, and Chatwoot, the open-source customer support platform, have published a joint case study. It shows how Tellus brought its own account tools and an in-house AI support analyst into the workspace its Customer Success team uses every day.

Tellus connected its in-app chat to a self-hosted, open-source customer support workspace.

Tellus runs Chatwoot Enterprise on its own infrastructure and connected it to the in-app chat its customers already use. The Customer Success team first answered customers from Chatwoot on August 4, 2026, eight days after writing its requirements. Tellus switched off its old ticket queue ten days later. Tellus engineers used AI coding assistance throughout the build.

What changed for Tellus's Customer Success team:

  • Account context in the conversation. Team members see the customer's profile, finances, Boosts and referrals in tabs beside each conversation. Each signs in under their own name.
  • An AI analyst for the team. Team members can ask CS-Lead, built on Tellus's own AI agent platform, why a payment failed or what a customer is seeing. CS-Lead gives signed-in team members account context, and controls filter specified identifiers from its answers. Team members decide what to send.
  • The same chat for customers. Customers kept using the in-app chat they already knew. A bridge carries each message to Chatwoot and each reply back.
  • Faster first replies as volume grew. In October, the median wait for a first reply from a person during support hours was 45% shorter than in May through July, before the switch. Across September and October it was 36% shorter, while total conversation volume grew about 30%.

"We treat customer support as an integral part of the product. Our customers trust us with their savings and their homes. They deserve answers that are fast and right, and our team now has their account and our own AI beside every conversation," said Jeromee (JJ) Johnson, President and CTO of Tellus. "Chatwoot gave us an open platform we could run ourselves and extend in a week."

Tellus runs Chatwoot itself, in an environment Tellus owns and controls rather than in Chatwoot's cloud. Team members reach it through the company VPN and single sign-on, and defined, authenticated integrations connect it to the services they need. In this workflow, the AI analyst has no tools to change customer accounts or to send messages to customers.

"Tellus shows what a strong engineering team can build on Chatwoot," said Pranav Raj Sreepuram, co-founder and CEO of Chatwoot. "They brought their own in-app chat, internal tools, and AI capabilities together in a single support workspace, all on infrastructure they control. This is exactly what we envisioned when building Chatwoot: an open platform that teams can customize and extend to fit their needs. We are proud to have Tellus as an Enterprise customer."

The case study, "How Tellus put its own tools and AI inside every Chatwoot conversation," is available at chatwoot.com/case-studies/tellus.

data.title: Digital Infrastructure World 2027 Announces First 85 Speakers as Registrants Represent 80GW of AI Buying Capacity

SAN JOSE, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 18, 2026 / Registration is now open for Digital Infrastructure World (DIW), the first and only event designed to unite the entire digital infrastructure stack-from IT to OT, spanning silicon, compute and networking through power, cooling, data center facilities and the grid. DIW brings these interconnected communities together for collaboration and conversation to address the rapidly evolving demands of artificial intelligence and next-generation digital infrastructure.

Produced by CloserStill Media in collaboration with the Open Compute Project Foundation (OCP), the inaugural event will take place February 2-4, 2027, at the San Jose Convention Center in San Jose, California.

Originally announced as a two-day event, Digital Infrastructure World has expanded to three days, opening Tuesday, February 2, with keynote presentation and welcome reception. The expanded format will provide additional opportunities for attendees to connect with industry leaders, explore emerging technologies and engage with the organizations shaping the future of AI infrastructure.

"AI is fundamentally changing how digital infrastructure is designed, deployed and operated, and the industry needs greater collaboration between the teams developing compute technologies and those responsible for powering, cooling and operating the facilities that support them," said Fran Pennella, Vice President, US Digital Infrastructure Portfolio, CloserStill Media. "Digital Infrastructure World is designed to bridge that gap by bringing the entire ecosystem together in one place. Our expanded three-day format, collaboration with the OCP organizing a collocated OCP Tech Day, and exceptional lineup of industry leaders will create a forum for practical conversations, meaningful partnerships and solutions that help organizations meet the growing demands of AI."

Digital Infrastructure World will feature keynote presentations and executive discussions with technology leaders representing organizations at the forefront of AI infrastructure, semiconductor innovation, computing systems and connectivity. Confirmed speakers on the program represent leading organizations including AMD, Arm, AWS, Broadcom, Crusoe, Digital Realty, Google, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, Schneider Electric, and Siemens.

These leaders will share insights into the evolving requirements of AI infrastructure, the convergence of computing and data center technologies, and the innovations needed to support increasingly complex, high-performance computing environments.

The conference program will feature four focused tracks addressing the critical technologies and challenges involved in designing, building, powering and operating next-generation AI infrastructure:

  • The Rack Track: Led by OCP, this track will explore the design of the 1-megawatt (MW) rack, from open rack architectures and silicon diversity to in-rack power distribution and advanced cooling technologies.
  • The Data Center Track: Focused on building the AI Data Center around the rack, this track will address liquid cooling, higher facility water temperatures, 800-volt DC and medium-voltage power distribution, and prefabricated solutions that accelerate construction. Hyperscalers, colocation providers and design-build engineers will share strategies for deploying high-density infrastructure efficiently and at scale.
  • The Cluster Track: Exploring how individual compute racks are combined to operate as a unified computing system, this track addresses scale-out and scale-across networking, optical connectivity, and the challenges of managing large-scale AI training and inference environments, including clusters with 1 million GPUs.
  • The Energy Track: Addressing AI's growing power demands, this track examines grid interconnection, on-site generation, battery storage, nuclear energy and grid integration. Industry experts will discuss strategies for accelerating access to power, managing fluctuating AI workloads and overcoming infrastructure constraints to support gigawatt-scale data center campuses.

The program will bring together hyperscalers, cloud providers, technology innovators, data center operators and infrastructure engineers to explore solutions that connect advances in silicon, computing and networking with the physical infrastructure required to deploy AI at scale.

A key component of the event is its collaboration with the OCP, a global nonprofit organization that accelerates innovation through open technologies and hyperscale best practices. The partnership combines OCP's global community of technology innovators, hyperscale operators and manufacturers with CloserStill Media's established network of data center operators, colocation providers and enterprise users.

Together, these communities will address critical infrastructure challenges and advance discussions aligned with OCP's Open Systems for AI Strategic Initiative, which focuses on accelerating the development and deployment of scalable AI infrastructure.

"Scaling AI Data Centers requires more than advances in computing performance. "Our collaborative mission and vision, Chip-to-Grid, and our partnership with Digital Infrastructure World bring these communities together to build the needed ecosystem, to accelerate open innovation, address infrastructure challenges and turn emerging technologies into practical, scalable solutions."

"That's (a half-point hike) only going to serve to accelerate the math on value compression and then that starts to hurt companies," said Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion.

Investors will scan the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting, due later on Wednesday, for clues on the central bank's policy path.

data.title: As criticism mounts, Trump administration says tech outages not coordinated
data.description:
* Clayton cites maintenance and technical changes in outages

* He does not see coordinated or state-sponsored attacks

By Doina Chiacu, Alexandra Alper and Mike Stone

WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The top US intelligence official said on Wednesday the disruptions to critical systems over the past week were not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack, as President Donald Trump's administration faces mounting criticism over its response.

Technology-related disruptions have hit every weekday between Thursday and Tuesday, including a nationwide halt to air travel, a Microsoft ( MSFT ) outage that hit email services and a temporary disruption to the US National Security Agency's network.

"I understand the timing of these incidents can raise questions, and it should. The American people should ask us these questions," Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told a House of Representatives Homeland Security Committee hearing on worldwide threats.

"But based on what we know today, after a great deal of diligence, these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes. They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack," Clayton said.

Clayton added that threats from Iran have substantially increased, though he did not link those to the spate of domestic outages.

The administration has struggled at times to give a unified message addressing growing worries among the public and in Congress, where some of the Republican president's allies have demanded more answers about what went wrong. Trump on Tuesday described the situations as "fine."

Experts worry that AI tools are feeding a surge of cyberactivity, with cybersecurity companies regularly turning up examples of hackers using AI to launch scores of intrusions at once.

QUESTIONS AROUND FLIGHT GROUNDING

At the House hearing, Democratic US Representative Bennie Thompson said it was irresponsible for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to board a private jet to attend a college football game last weekend amid the transportation disruptions.

"The so-called leadership of the Trump administration consists of refusing to take responsibility, shifting blame to the others, and putting your own interests above the country," Thompson said.

Mullin defended the administration's handling of the ground stop as "a success" given that thousands of planes landed safely before flights resumed, and said that changing his plans could have led some to worry that he doubted it was safe to fly.

Officials have said the installation of a router in Arkansas triggered the ground stop, the longest such halt to air travel since the al Qaeda attacks on the United States on September 11, 2001.

The recent incidents also included a disruption to some JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) banking activities, a United Airlines technology failure that delayed about 150 flights and an Apple ( AAPL ) outage that affected customer services including iCloud and Apple Pay.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking to reporters in Manila on Wednesday, acknowledged that the incidents were "unsettling" but said they were completely unrelated and there was "zero evidence" they were caused by "nefarious actors."

(Additional reporting by Doborah Mary Sophia in New York, Alyssa Pointer in Atlanta and Trevor Hunnicutt in Manila; Writing by Jonathan Spicer; editing by Scott Malone and Will Dunham)

data.title: StepSecurity Raises $20 Million in Series A Funding to Prevent Supply Chain Attacks
data.description:
Launches free Secure Registry community tier, making protection accessible to open-source maintainers

SEATTLE, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- StepSecurity, the cybersecurity company that prevents supply chain attacks, today announced an oversubscribed $20 million round of Series A funding. In combination with a previous seed funding round of $3 million, this brings the total of funding raised to date to $23 million. The round was led by Elephant, with participation from existing investors Runtime Ventures, Inner Loop Capital, and SaaS Ventures. With this funding, StepSecurity will accelerate the development and distribution of its comprehensive platform, which combines developer-machine protection, repository checks, Secure Registry, and Harden-Runner for CI/CD to block malicious packages at all control points in the agentic software pipeline.

"We founded StepSecurity in 2021 because we wanted security teams to have visibility and protection in the environments where software gets built," said Varun Sharma, Co-founder and CEO, StepSecurity. "With this Series A funding, we enter our next phase of growth with years of experience protecting development environments, a solid foundation of trust earned through open-source expertise, and a host of advanced products shaped by real supply chain attacks."

Recent software supply chain attacks have increasingly weaponized malicious packages, automated installation hooks, and hijacked developer accounts to target popular ecosystems like npm, IDE extensions, and AI agents. The need to secure development environments has never been more urgent, as illustrated by recent high-profile security breaches:

  • The $6.3 Billion Breach at Binance (October 2026): A threat actor, whom the FBI has identified as North Korea's TraderTraitor group, compromised a developer's laptop to access an internal service container with the permissions to initiate withdrawal requests. Using that access as a starting point, the attackers exploited additional points of compromise and an Ethereum account-delegation mechanism to gain transaction approval authority over a hot wallet. In around 20 minutes, the threat actors drained billions of dollars in assets.
  • Claude Code Extension Tampering (October 2026): A tampered copy of the Claude Code extension was served on the Cursor Extension Marketplace for several hours to deploy a persistent SSH backdoor.
  • The Shai-Hulud Attack Series (2025-2026): Attackers hijacked developer credentials and pushed hundreds of malicious packages via a major, self-replicating software supply chain worm and cyberattack campaign targeting the open-source npm and PyPI ecosystems.

The StepSecurity platform combines developer-machine protection, repository checks, Secure Registry, and Harden-Runner for CI/CD. With StepSecurity, a malicious component that gets past one layer will still be detected or blocked at another. "We believe independent controls at all control points in agentic software pipelines are the strongest defense for agentic software development," explained Ashish Kurmi, Co-founder and CTO, StepSecurity. "We have seen our customers adopt one product, find value, and ask us to protect the next part of their development process. This funding gives us the resources to respond faster."

The Series A will help StepSecurity to invest in three strategic areas: 

  1. Product and engineering. StepSecurity will grow its engineering team, deepen its existing products, and extend protection to the environments customers are asking to secure, including agent sandboxes. 
  2. Security research. Expanding StepSecurity's research team's ability will enable the company to discover attacks early, investigate their impact, and turn those findings into actionable protection. 
  3. Go-to-Market: To keep pace with growing demand and help more organizations adopt StepSecurity, the company is expanding its go-to-market efforts.

More than 20,000 open-source projects use the free community tier of StepSecurity's Harden-Runner. On the commercial side, StepSecurity's ARR grew 5x in 2024 and 5x again in 2025. In 2026, the company has already surpassed 5x growth and is on pace for its strongest year yet. Enterprise customers including Circle, Dexcom, Kong, Mercari, Chainguard, and XBOW rely on StepSecurity's enterprise platform to protect their software supply chains. "With the increase in supply chain attacks, StepSecurity gives us peace of mind that this behavior will be caught and stopped." said Ryan Richardson, SOC Lead, Utility Warehouse.

In addition to its Series A funding, StepSecurity is launching a free Secure Registry community tier, integrated with Harden-Runner. This offering extends StepSecurity's commitment to making protection accessible to open-source maintainers. Now, any public repository using Harden-Runner can pull packages through Secure Registry and block compromised packages.

"We're thrilled to invest in and partner with StepSecurity, a company that has taken an innovative approach to tackling the enormous issue of supply chain attacks," said Matt Tanenblatt, Partner, Elephant. "Under the leadership of Varun and Ashish, the team has created a category-defining platform that ensures that malicious packages will not make their way past key control points. This helps security teams address the problem before the damage is done. With applicability to almost any security organization, the market for this solution is enormous and growing quickly."

About StepSecurity

StepSecurity prevents software supply chain attacks. Its platform secures every stage of software development, from developer machines and AI coding agents to code repositories, package registries, and CI/CD runners, so malicious code is detected and blocked before it can do damage. It was founded in 2021 by security veterans from Microsoft, Uber, and Plaid. For more information or to get started, please visit https://stepsecurity.io
